- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.50), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if price has recently fallen sharply.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 3–7 days post-spike.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast by 1–4% for next 7 days.  
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 3–5 consecutive days of high prices); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for 3–7 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic in early days (days 1–7); apply a “lag correction”: subtract 0.5–2% from forecast for days 1–7 if sentiment is neutral or bearish.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “bullish → bearish” transitions, model often fails to anticipate reversal; apply a “reversal buffer”: add 1–3% to forecast for 3–5 days after sentiment turns bearish.
